newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's UNITA deserts U.N. camp in diamond area.
newsitem.headline: Angola's UNITA deserts U.N. camp in diamond area.

text.p: Angolan former rebel UNITA troops, awaiting demobilisation at a U.N.-run camp in the northeast, have abandoned the site after clashes nearby between UNITA and the government, a U.N. official said on Monday.
"There is no doubt that the Muchinda camp is empty. Apparently UNITA has abandoned the area," Carlo Scaramella of the U.N.'s humanitarian agency (UCAH) told Reuters.
The agency is one of the main groups overseeing the demobilisation of 100,000 UNITA and government troops in terms of a 1994 peace treaty between both sides to end two decades of civil war.
"The U.N. is considering closing down the area as there is is no way we can carry out demobilisation because there is no one there," Scaramella added.
The Muchinda camp, located in the diamond-rich Lunda Norte province, is one of 14 assembly sites set up by the U.N. to disarm UNITA troops under the 1994 peace agreement.
Around 4,500 UNITA troops were disarmed at Muchinda since last year, but since clashes erupted a month ago the troops have slowly deserted the site.
Aid officials working in the camp told Reuters the troops had said they were leaving to protect their families against government advances.
The government's army launched an offensive against UNITA-held areas in the northeast in May to retake diamond territory captured by UNITA during the civil war.
Although both sides were joined in a unity government in April, UNITA refuses to let go of its 80 percent stake in the country's diamond wealth.
